articles.title: Super League Grand Final: Wakefield Trinity make history with 23-10 victory over Warrington Wolves
articles.summary: Wakefield Trinity were crowned Super League champions for the first time in the club's history with a 23-10 victory over Warrington Wolves in the Grand Final at Old Trafford.
articles.body:
Wakefield Trinity become the sixth team to win Super League; they have done it on the first time of asking; it finishes off a remarkable story after they were relegated in 2023

Wakefield Trinity were crowned Super League champions for the first time in the club's history with a 23-10 victory over Warrington Wolves in the Grand Final at Old Trafford.

It is the first time Wakefield have made the Grand Final and they achieved their greatest glory on their first attempt.

They also become the sixth winner of Super League, joining Wigan Warriors, St Helens, Leeds Rhinos, Bradford Bulls and Hull KR.

It rounds out a fairy-tale story for Wakefield who were relegated in 2023, returned to Super League in the 2025 season, and have now written themselves into the history books as champions.

Wakefield held a dominant 19-0 half-time lead thanks to converted tries from Cameron Scott, Isaiah Vagana and Jazz Tevaga, Max Jowitt staying calm under pressure with the boot.

The extra point was then added by Jack Sinfield with just minutes left in the first half.

Early in the second half there was drama as Corey Hall was sent to the sin bin for a high shot on Arron Lindop. Lindop scored with Wakefield a player down, and added a second later on, Ewan Irwin converting the first.

However, a try from Trinity winger Tom Johnstone was enough for them to stay far enough ahead and seal immortality.

Johnstone picked up the Rob Burrow Award for his phenomenal display in both attack and defence.

Wakefield complete the fairy tale with stunning Grand Final win

In front of an electric and sold-out Old Trafford, it was a flawless first 40 from Wakefield Trinity.

They thought they had opened the scoring on the sixth minute when Johnstone went over in the corner. However, on review, it was clear he had been held up then forced into touch.

It took only six minutes longer though for the Yorkshire side to get on the board thanks to a sublime no-look, one-handed flick pass from Lachlan Walmsley which sent Scott walking in and with the Jowitt conversion, they had a 6-0 lead.

While it was end-to-end stuff, metres were coming much more easily to Wakefield with their pack proving too strong. That meant every set ended in pressure.

In the 25th minute, a brilliant Jake Trueman pressure kick saw Johnstone jump highest and find Vagana on his shoulder to walk in. Jowitt added the extras once again.

Just over 10 minutes later, Tyson Smoothy went close and then was followed by Tevaga who threw a dummy and then used his power to barrel over. Jowitt stayed perfect with the boot to extend Wakefield's lead further.

With less than two minutes remaining of the opening half, Jack Sinfield used some big-game nous to send over a drop goal to give Wakefield a more than three-score lead, and left Warrington with a mountain to climb at 19-0 down.

There was drama immediately in the second half when Wakefield's Corey Hall was sent to the sin bin for a high shot on Arron Lindop to give Warrington their opportunity to hit back, and they did.

Irwin threw a lovely dummy and then passed to open up the space and with a player advantage, Lindop had all the room to walk over in front of the Warrington faithful. Irwin converted to bring the scoreline to 19-6.

Warrington thought they had gone in again through Matty Ashton just minutes later, but a forward pass ruled out what would have been a score that brought the game right back in the balance

However, with numerical parity restored, it did not take long for Wakefield to get back on top once again and off the back of huge metres from Caleb Hamlin-Uele, they sent it out to Johnstone who used his step to pull off a sensational finish and with a 23-6 lead and 20 minutes to play, the Wakefield end was bouncing.

Warrington would not give up and with eight minutes left on the clock they kept the last tackle alive; Irwin sent over a looping pass and Lindop was in for his second. However, this time Irwin could not convert and the score was 23-10.

However the clock quickly ran away, Wakefield stayed strong, and immortality was theirs as the full-time hooter went and their name was etched onto the Super League trophy.

Jowitt: A rollercoaster of a year for me - highs are worth the lows

"A million per cent the highs are worth the lows.

"It didn't feel real that we were playing a Grand Final until we got here today.

"A rollercoaster of a year for me personally after dropping down to the reserves, not finding form, but I got my opportunity at the back end of the year.

"For this to be my last game for Wakefield, I will never forget it."

'Emotional' Johnstone: I can't believe it - my dream for the last decade!

Rob Burrow Award winner Tom Johnstone to Sky Sports:

"I can't quite believe it. I keep crying, I can't help myself! Such a special club, it's been the longest week of my life.

"To get out there and get it done, I don't know what to say.

"This club means eveyrthing to me. I've been saying it for a long time. My dream the last 10 years was to win a Grand Final with Wakefield.

"Daryl Powell sold me the dream that we were a club that had aspirations and wanted to win things.

"I believed every word they said and this is where we are now.

"We don't do this without that belief we have. We built our foundation on that."

Powell: We have produced flawless rugby league and will get better

Wakefield Trinity head coach Daryl Powell to Sky Sports:

"It's unbelievable really, the story. Where we've come from and our ability to go toe-to-toe with the best teams in the comp.

"We had a bit of a rocky period with the 10-minute sin-binning, but we were superb today.

"That's a big performance from an unbelievable group of blokes.

"We just kept talking about it, and the players have gradually developed and got better. Then it becomes a reality when they see what they are capable of.

"Last week and the start today, almost three flawless halves of rugby league.

"We went to Wigan last week, and that was a hell of a job to go there and win, and it showed us what we could do.

"We kept that belief coming into this game. We are a proper team and we're going to get better."

Burgess: They beat us physically - it hurts

Warrington Wolves head coach Sam Burgess to Sky Sports:

"The stats were relatively similar in terms of possession and completion, but they beat us physically.

"They've [Wakefield] had a red-hot finish to the season.

"I'm very proud of my group, as it quite easily could have got messy today. We stuck together. But it hurts.

"I don't think I'll have any regrets. We showed a lot of spirit in the second half. We are disappointed no doubt. But regrets? No.

"It was Wakefield's day today .The challenge is to now take that next step. It will be a long few weeks away."

articles.title: "He grabbing our wives by the a–" - Charles Barkley recalls wild New Year's Eve party with Mike Tyson
articles.summary: Barkley’s New Year’s Eve party became an unforgettable night after Mike Tyson showed up.
articles.body:
After 16 years in the NBA, a Hall of Fame career and years as one of basketball's most prominent broadcasters, Charles Barkley has built relationships and shared plenty of memorable moments with high-profile figures.

These encounters with celebrities have made for stories that some might find hard to believe. On "New Heights," Barkley shared one such story in vivid detail, recalling the time Mike Tyson got into some trouble at a New Year's party he hosted.

"Mike Tyson was actually one of my neighbors up the street for about four or five years. And so he would always come around," Barkley said . "I have a New Year's Eve party every year. So, one year Mike comes. Mike came a couple years."

Guests complained to Barkley about Tyson's behavior

Barkley invited a group of about 40 to 50 people and had a strict no-pictures and no-autographs rule, allowing everyone to relax and enjoy the night without the usual celebrity attention. As the guests partied, drank and enjoyed themselves while DJs blasted music, Tyson arrived.

As if Tyson needed any introduction, Barkley recalled that the boxer announced his presence through a loud bullhorn, telling everyone, "The champ is here." It was quite the entrance, but Barkley quickly reminded him that he was not the only celebrity in the room.

About two hours into the party, Tyson began making some attendees uncomfortable, according to Barkley. The former Phoenix Suns star said several husbands eventually approached with a concern about Tyson's behavior

"Three or four of the husbands come up to me and says, 'Yo, man, you got to do something about Mike.' I said, 'What's Mike doing?'" Barkley asked. "He says, 'He grabbing our wife by the a–.' He was going around grabbing women."

During his NBA career, Barkley had his fair share of brawls and altercations. He was also a strong physical specimen who battled against giants inside the paint despite being undersized. But he was well aware of the reputation of Tyson, who also once threatened Barkley .

"Let me get this straight. The guy who bit a guy ear off. Y'all want me to go and confront him?" he said.

Barkely was understandably hesitant, but as the host, he ultimately obliged.

"So, I walked up. 'Hey, Mike, there's only a couple women here who are single. Not that you should be grabbing their a– either, but most of the women here bought a date,'" he said. "And he's like, 'Okay, Charles… You're right. I'll stop doing that.' I said, 'I'd appreciate it.'"

Barkley thought he was done dealing with Tyson, but he was wrong. Later into the party, the legendary power forward started smelling marijuana in the restaurant, prompting him to look for the source. Sure enough, the strong odor led him to Tyson, smoking in a corner.

Like what he did earlier, he ultimately asked Tyson to stop, expressing his concern for how his actions could affect the business establishment and potentially cost it its food and beverage license.

"Can you not smoke?" Barkley recalled asking.

Once again, Tyson agreed to Barkley's request, saying that he didn't want that to happen. He stopped smoking inside before finding another place to continue smoking. At that point, Barkley decided to just let him be.

"About 30 minutes later, you know, Mike's out on the front. You know how some restaurants have like a little bench? Mike out front of the restaurant just blazing away," Barkley said, "I say, 'Hey, man, leave the dude alone.' He was always cordial, though, but he was interesting."

Barkley has countless celebrity stories to tell, but this New Year's Eve encounter with Tyson is forever stuck with him.

articles.title: Cristiano cambia los planes
articles.standfirst: Retabet ofrece las cuotas de Portugal para la UEFA Nations League y para la Eurocopa, alteradas tras la salida del luso del conjunto luso
articles.summary: Retabet ofrece las cuotas de Portugal para la UEFA Nations League y para la Eurocopa, alteradas tras la salida del luso del conjunto luso
articles.body: Pocas veces un partido de la selección portuguesa ha dejado tantas dudas fuera del campo como los últimos días. La salida de Cristiano Ronaldo de la concentración, en plena Nations League y con su posible retirada internacional sobre la mesa, sacude a la campeona en título y ha hecho que las casas de apuestas contemplen como sus mercados a largo plazo, en lo que a la selección portuguesa se refiere, se hayan visto modificados. Todo empezó el domingo, cuando Portugal ganó 2-1 a Noruega y Cristiano vio todo el partido desde el banquillo, pese a haber calentado durante la segunda parte. Jorge Jesus, su antiguo entrenador en Al Nassr, admitió que el delantero estaba decepcionado, y el miércoles anunció en rueda de prensa que tampoco contaría con él ante Dinamarca. Horas después, el jugador abandonó la concentración de Copenhague. Según el diario 'O Jogo', la decisión es irreversible y su último partido habría sido el de Gales. El mercado a corto plazo refleja de la siguiente manera la salida de Cristiano Ronaldo. Retabet paga la victoria de Portugal en el próximo partido ante Noruega a 1.64, frente a 4.24 del empate y 4.44 del triunfo visitante. Noruega, que cayó ante Portugal por la mínima y llega con dos derrotas seguidas, parte con menos crédito. Más lejos, el panorama de las apuestas deportivas en Retabet cambia. Portugal es tercera favorita para repetir título de Nations League a 6.55 (probabilidad implícita cercana al 15 %), por detrás de España, a 3.78, y Francia, a 4.04. No es una sorpresa. Ambos rivales llegan con plantillas muy sólidas y un arranque casi perfecto. Pero conviene fijarse en la distancia. Portugal se queda a casi tres puntos de cuota de España, lo que sugiere que el mercado aplica un descuento por la inestabilidad del vestuario y la incertidumbre sobre cómo digerirá el grupo el conflicto con su estrella. La foto es parecida en la Eurocopa de 2028. Portugal aparece como cuarta favorita a 8.05, por detrás de Francia y España, ambas a 5.05, e Inglaterra, a 5.55. La brecha con las dos primeras es mayor que en la Nations League, algo lógico. A casi dos años vista, el mercado pondera más la renovación generacional que la actualidad. Una Portugal sin Cristiano en 2028 tendría que sostenerse en Bruno Fernandes, Vitinha, Nuno Mendes, João Neves y la nueva hornada de delanteros, un núcleo con calidad de sobra, pero sin un goleador de referencia consolidado. En definitiva, el 'caso Cristiano' es, por ahora, más un problema de vestuario que de rendimiento. El mercado lo refleja con claridad: Portugal sigue siendo gran favorita ante Noruega, tercera opción para repetir título de Nations League y cuarta de cara a la Eurocopa de 2028. Sin embargo, la incertidumbre tiene un precio.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Week 4 Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: Justin Boone's lineup advice
articles.summary: Justin Boone helps you set those lineups for fantasy football in Week 4.
articles.body:
Justin Boone provides a weekly look at undervalued fantasy players to consider starting this week and potential busts you might want to leave on your bench.

For the rest of your lineup decisions, consult his Week 4 rankings .

Shough is off to an impressive start, posting the fourth-most fantasy points among quarterbacks so far. That includes very consistent production with weekly finishes as the QB6, QB8 and QB6 through three games.

After fielding the fastest-paced offense last season, Kellen Moore has picked up where he left off. The Saints are nearly a full second quicker in neutral pace of play, which leads to plenty of volume for Shough and company.

We're set up for a Monday night shootout, with a Falcons team that looked much more competitive with Michael Penix Jr. under center last week. Atlanta's defense is giving up the 12th-most fantasy points to passers and had to place its best cornerback A.J. Terrell on injured reserve. You can confidently project another QB1 result from Shough.

Jared Goff at Panthers – Speaking of corners heading to IR, Carolina just lost both Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson for at least the next four weeks and possibly longer. Even though we tend to avoid Goff when he's outdoors, we'll make an exception here in a game that's tied for the highest projected point total on the week at 51.5.

Bryce Young vs. Lions – Young is on the other side of that contest and facing a Lions defense that's been without several starters. Unsurprisingly, that's led to Detroit allowing the most fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks this year. Young is positioned well for his third top-12 finish on the season.

Love is fresh off a breakout game against the 49ers, where he put up 109 scrimmage yards and a receiving touchdown on 26 touches. That was by far his strongest usage of the season (64% snap share) and a sign of things to come for the third overall pick.

We might have even seen this happen sooner if it wasn't for his preseason ankle injury, but fantasy managers who drafted him in the third round aren't complaining now.

Next up is a potential positive game script against a Giants defense that's given up the 10th-most fantasy points to running backs this season, including Javonte Williams (72 yards, two TDs), Kyren Williams (97 yards, one TD), Blake Corum (92 yards) and Tony Pollard (96 yards). Get ready for a big week from Love, who is a top-10 RB in my rest-of-season trade value charts .

Aaron Jones Sr. vs. Dolphins – Jones, who turns 32 in December, can't hold up to massive workloads forever, but he should do well against a Miami team that's allowed the most fantasy points to running backs, including top-five finishes in each of the first three weeks.

Braelon Allen at Bears – Breece Hall is sidelined, opening the door for the 22-year-old Allen, who's flashed on his limited touches. Chicago's defense has permitted at least 80 scrimmage yards to every starting RB its played.

Jacory Croskey-Merritt vs. Colts (London) – Rachaad White is dealing with a shoulder injury that could keep him out this week. That may leave the recently signed Austin Ekeler and rookie Kaytron Allen as the only backups behind JCM. As I wrote about in my trade tips column , Bill is being underrated after a 48-yard TD was called back on an illegal formation penalty last week. I'm excited to see what he can do against a Colts defense that's the sixth-easiest matchup for RBs.

Golden is tied for the seventh-most targets per game through three weeks, just ahead of his teammate Christian Watson. While both players are performing well, Watson has received significantly more praise and sits as the WR3 overall in fantasy points per game. However, Golden isn't far behind at WR14.

With the current state of Green Bay's offense, Watson and Golden are going to remain busy. The Packers have lost Jayden Reed for the season, Tucker Kraft is still working his way back to form after last year's ACL tear and the run game is non-existent.

At the moment, Golden is looking like one of the best fantasy picks you could have made this summer. Expect his strong production to continue against Tampa's pass funnel defense.

Josh Downs at Commanders (London) – With Alec Pierce sidelined, the Colts have finally turned up the volume for Downs, who has 20 targets, 12 catches and 149 yards over the last two games. Now, he squares off with a Commanders secondary that's allowed the most fantasy points to receivers.

Michael Wilson at Giants – After posting his best stat line of the young season (11-89-1 on 17 targets!), Wilson gets his easiest matchup so far in Week 4. The Giants defense has been responsible for a top-20 WR finish in each of the first three weeks and Wilson is next.

Jameson Williams at Panthers – A high-scoring game against a defense that's missing its top two corners sounds like the perfect get-right spot for Williams. This will be a spike-week for the Lions' boom-or-bust wideout.

Johnson has been an excellent late-round selection and an extremely consistent fantasy starter in the opening month. Among tight ends, he's fifth in receptions, sixth in yards and tied for first with three touchdowns. That's helped generate TE7, TE13 and TE5 weekly finishes.

A friendly matchup with the Falcons awaits in Week 4. Atlanta is the seventh-most generous defense to fantasy tight ends, including allowing a league-high three touchdowns to the position through three games.

Jordyn Tyson has one more week on IR and isn't immediately expected back, so Johnson will continue to be a strong fantasy TE1.

Kenyon Sadiq at Bears – Following his seven-catch, 105-yard, one-touchdown breakout last week, Sadiq has been limited in practice with a back injury. As long as he's healthy, he'll be a top-12 TE option, with Adonai Mitchell and Mason Taylor still week-to-week.

Darren Waller vs. Lions – Waller gets to take on the same Detroit defense that was responsible for Sadiq's massive stat line in Week 3. Not only are the Lions giving up the most fantasy points to the position, they've allowed six touchdowns to tight ends in three weeks. If Jalen Coker is limited or ruled out, that would push Waller even higher up my rankings.

During his rookie season, in the nine outings where Maye played at least 85% of the snaps, he never finished lower than QB17. Last year, we saw him combine that high floor with a high ceiling and he finished as the QB3 overall in fppg, while scoring less than 14 fantasy points only one time.

This season, he's been under 13 fantasy points in all three outings and currently sits as the QB35.

Yes, there have been injuries to A.J. Brown and the offensive line. The matchups have also been tougher (Seahawks, Steelers, Jaguars) after having an easier schedule in 2025. However, it's still hard to explain the disappearance of Maye's once high floor.

Even against a softer opponent in the Bills, it's hard to trust Maye in your lineup until we see him turn this around. Though Buffalo allowed four TDs to Jared Goff, they held C.J. Stroud and Justin Herbert to QB15 and QB23 finishes, respectively.

I'm not dropping Maye, but I am sending him to my bench in the leagues where I have a decent streaming option.

Justin Herbert at Seahawks – Herbert is also on the list of quarterbacks who have been massive disappointments in September. This doesn't look like a bounce-back week with Ladd McConkey's status uncertain and the Seahawks' defense waiting for them in Seattle.

Bo Nix at 49ers – Nix finally stepped up for fantasy managers last week, in part thanks to a rushing touchdown. They all count though. We'll see if he can get the Broncos into scoring position as frequently against a 49ers defense allowing the eighth-fewest fantasy points to QBs.

Hampton has been unspectacular in the early part of the season, saving his fantasy performances in the first two weeks by scoring touchdowns. That's important since his role in the passing game is limited and potentially shrinking.

Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal had their usage increase, resulting in Hampton only running a route on 16% of the dropbacks in Week 3. While I'm not concerned about his job security, it is worrisome that we might be talking about a three-man committee in an offense that's stumbled so far.

The Seahawks aren't a defense to target either, since they're giving up the fifth-fewest points to runners. The schedule also doesn't relent for the next couple months with matchups against the Broncos, Chiefs, Rams, Texans and Ravens.

Hampton might have to be started depending on your roster, but he's more of a TD-or-bust RB3 right now.

Rhamondre Stevenson at Bills – Stevenson might be slightly undervalued in terms of his rest-of-season value, since his usage rebounded after fumbling in Week 2. Unfortunately, he's another ball-carrier sharing his backfield in a struggling offense. He's a TD-or-bust RB3 in a game where the Pats could fall behind quickly.

Tony Pollard at Ravens – While the Ravens have given up solid stat lines to the likes of Jonathan Taylor and Javonte Williams, we can project the same for Pollard in a game the Titans will likely trail. Scoring opportunities are also few and far between for Tennessee.

J.K. Dobbins at 49ers – Dobbins has been held to 36 yards, 36 yards and 53 yards during his first three appearances this season. He only caught one pass and has yet to visit the end zone. He's just a low-ceiling fantasy option, with RJ Harvey soaking up all the pass-catching work.

Through three weeks, Egbuka's numbers haven't been terrible, especially when you consider the overall state of the Bucs' offense. Stat lines of 5-63-0, 3-16-1 and 5-62-0 aren't going to destroy your chances of winning a fantasy week, but they aren't going to lead you to victory either.

Now, he'll have to build on those performances without the help of Baker Mayfield for the next few weeks. Jalon Daniels is an intriguing rookie backup, but expecting him to improve this offense is wishful thinking.

So even in a positive matchup with the Packers, I have Egbuka ranked as a volatile WR3/flex option.

Ladd McConkey/Quentin Johnston at Seahawks – McConkey was seen walking around the locker room with a limp after being downgraded to DNP for Thursday's practice. Even if he suits up, the injury and matchup with the Seahawks is enough for me to bench him. Meanwhile, Johnston has been so bad this year that he would just be a risky WR3/flex option if McConkey sits out. Tre' Harris is an intriguing stash though.

Rome Odunze vs. Jets – The Bears' passing game is being split four ways instead of three now that Kalif Raymond has a legitimate role. Odunze's average depth of target is nearly double his fellow receivers and he isn't getting many of the easy targets. That makes him a TD-or-bust WR4/flex.

Xavier Worthy at Raiders – Worthy hasn't topped 25 yards this season. A big play is possible at any point, but he's a very dangerous flex swing with an extremely low floor for fantasy managers.

It turns out other defensive coordinators get to watch prior game film and after seeing Schultz catch 12 passes for 140 yards in Week 2, the Colts made it a priority to cover him last Sunday. The result was just three targets, three receptions and 30 yards.

With Nico Collins expected to return this week, the volume scam for Schultz is over. The Cowboys have also held every tight end other than Isaiah Likely under 25 yards.

While Schultz can still be started as a lower-end TE2 streamer, you should be able to find a better option.

Colston Loveland vs. Jets – Loveland isn't commanding the immense target share he had down the stretch last season. With the Bears being content to spread the ball around more, Loveland is just a risky TE2 until we see otherwise. New York's defense hasn't given up a touchdown to tight ends yet, with 44 yards being the highest output against it.

Kyle Pitts Sr. at Saints – When Drake London is healthy, Pitts is an afterthought in the Falcons' passing attack. His stat lines of 0-0-0, 1-15-0 and 1-5-0 should have been reason enough for you to drop him this week.

Warrington Wolves head coach Sam Burgess to Sky Sports:

"The stats were relatively similar in terms of possession and completion, but they beat us physically.

"They've [Wakefield] had a red-hot finish to the season.

"I'm very proud of my group, as it quite easily could have got messy today. We stuck together. But it hurts.

"I don't think I'll have any regrets. We showed a lot of spirit in the second half. We are disappointed no doubt. But regrets? No.

"It was Wakefield's day today .The challenge is to now take that next step. It will be a long few weeks away."

articles.title: Harmanpreet Singh leads the charge as India tear through Malaysia 5-1 for Asian Games men's hockey gold; seal LA28 Olympics spot
articles.summary: The Indian men's hockey team defended their Asian Games gold medal and secured a spot at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics after defeating Malaysia 5-1 in the
articles.body: The Indian men's hockey team defended their Asian Games gold medal and secured a spot at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics after defeating Malaysia 5-1 in the final in Kakamigahara, Japan, on Saturday.India had never won successive Asian Games gold medals, making Saturday's final an opportunity to create history. Harmanpreet Singh-led India made the most of it as they successfully defended their title.Malaysia secured the silver, while Pakistan won the bronze by defeating South Korea 5-3 earlier in the day.India started slowly as Malaysia, as expected, defended in a low block and managed to keep the Indian attack out despite the pressure. India eventually broke the deadlock in the 12th minute through Harmanpreet.India won their first penalty corner after Hardik played Abhishek into the circle and the forward found a Malaysian defender's foot. Harmanpreet took the first attempt, but the push from Hardik was poor. India, however, won another penalty corner.Harmanpreet made no mistake with his second chance. The trap was better this time and he beat the first rusher with his drag-flick before sending a powerful shot past the goalkeeper, who could not see it to put India in the lead.Malaysia responded quickly and equalised just two minutes later in the 14th minute. Shello Silverius thrashed a half volley into the roof of the net from the left end of the circle. He received an aerial ball from the right and got his shot away almost immediately.The first quarter ended 1-1.India regained the lead in the 23rd minute through another penalty corner. Shilanand Lakra received the ball on the left wing and found a chance to enter the circle, but the attack was stopped. Soon after, Lakra made another run into the circle and this time won a foul.Jugraj Singh converted the penalty corner to put India 2-1 ahead.Malaysia continued to press India and put the defending champions under pressure, but India held on to their lead at half-time.India extended their advantage in the 42nd minute when Hardik Singh scored from another penalty corner. The goalkeeper moved to his right early, allowing Hardik to place the ball centrally and make it 3-1 for India.India exerted their dominance in the last few minutes as Abhishek scored another goal for India in the 55th minute to make it 4-1. Harmanpreet followed soon after to score his second goal of the match through penalty corner with a rocket drag-flick flying into the top left of the goal to put India into a comfortable 5-1 lead.India held on to complete a 5-1 victory over Malaysia and successfully defend their Asian Games title. articles.body: India finished fourth at the Asian Games 2026 in Nagoya on Saturday after a late surge of gold medals helped the country move into the top five. The star-studded cricket and hockey teams defended their titles as 17-year-old archer Kumkum Mohod and golfer Pranavi Urs emerged as the standout stories of India's campaign.India could not match the 106 medals they won at the previous edition, but finished with 85 medals, including 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze. In Kakamigahara, the Harmanpreet Singh-led hockey team defeated Malaysia 5-1 in the final to defend its Asian Games title. The gold also secured India direct qualification for the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles.Wrestler Aman Sehrawat was another Indian gold medallist on Saturday. The Olympic bronze-medallist won the 57kg category to add another Asian Games title to his achievements. He had won bronze in the same category at the Hangzhou 2022 edition.However, Kumkum and Pranavi were the standout stories of the day.Kumkum became the first Indian woman archer to win an individual recurve gold at the Asian Games, while Pranavi became the first Indian woman golfer to win an individual gold. articles.title: FSU softball opens fall ball with 19-5 win over Chipola
articles.summary: Freshmen Callee Leffler and McLaine Hudson drove in runs as FSU’s new-look roster scored 19 runs in its first fall scrimmage.
articles.body:
Florida State softball opened its fall season with a 19-5 scrimmage win over Chipola College on Oct. 2 at JoAnne Graf Field at the Seminole Softball Complex. The teams played 10 innings, three more than usual, after agreeing to extra innings for more practice time.

The scrimmage offered the first look at a Seminoles roster rebuilt after a 52-10 season in which they swept the Atlantic Coast Conference regular-season and tournament titles before falling in the Tallahassee Regional.

With shortstop Isa Torres, D1Softball's National Player of the Year, and infielder Jaysoni Beachum both transferring this offseason, FSU is filling the left side of its infield with a mix of transfers and freshmen.

The first inning was scoreless before Chipola freshman Jazmine Garcia scored in the top of the second to give the visitors a 1-0 lead.

FSU answered in the bottom of the inning. Sophomore Makenna Sturgis lined a hit to center field to tie the game, and freshman Callee Leffler drove in a second run before freshman infielder McLaine Hudson added an RBI double. Leffler then scored on a groundout by sophomore infielder Marin Heller to put the 'Noles up 4-1 after two innings.

After a brief weather delay, play resumed in the top of the third inning.

"It's awesome being back in the park. This is one of the premiere programs in the country and every time I come here I am reminded of it," Garnet and Gold fan Corey Neil said in an interview with the FSView after the game. "The facilities are second to none and it really is just so great to be back watching some FSU softball."

articles.title: ‘They Believe in the Product’ – NFL Insider Reveals Patriots’ Plan for Drake Maye
articles.summary: Despite being the NFL MVP runner-up last year, Drake Maye has had a somewhat sluggish, error-prone start to the 2026 season. The Patriots quarterback’s gamep...
articles.body:
Despite being the NFL MVP runner-up last year, Drake Maye has had a somewhat sluggish, error-prone start to the 2026 season. The Patriots quarterback's gameplay has taken a nosedive, with an abysmal passer rating of 58.6.

To pull Maye out of this situation, head coach Mike Vrabel was rethinking his approach. According to him, Maye appeared to be trying to do too much, forcing the issue and "choking the life out of the club," according to Vrabel.

Jeremy Fowler Discloses Patriots' Best Strategy for Drake Maye

ESPN insider Jeremy Fowler shed light on the team's strategy for their quarterback on Saturday.

"A topic of conversation in New England is will they simplify the offense a little bit. Mike Vrabel hinted at that this week. Do they need to quote "do less and do it better," asked the host.

Fowler replied, "Now, I talked to a source in New England who pushed back on that a little bit. Said that Maye did great in the offense last year. He knows Josh McDaniels' scheme. It's really about poor decision-making right now. It's also about confidence and some footwork issues. So they're trying to dig into that. They believe in the product. They're hoping he turns it around."

To support Maye, Vrabel silenced the press chatter earlier this week, saying , "Let me just tell you why I'm here. I'm here because Drake was the quarterback," Vrabel said. "Believe it or not, I had choices as to where I wanted to coach. I wanted to coach here because Drake was the quarterback. So, I don't have really much other to add to that about a comment from an unnamed source. But I'll just tell you what I've told numerous people if they want to ask me why I'm here."

The New England Patriots will play the Buffalo Bills in Week 4.

articles.title: Ex-Cowboys QB Reveals How Troy Aikman Used To Rip Him After Bad Play Calls
articles.summary: Troy Aikman was the Dallas Cowboys‘ starting quarterback during one of the best stretches in franchise history. Jason Garrett spent those same years mostly w...
articles.body:
Troy Aikman was the Dallas Cowboys ' starting quarterback during one of the best stretches in franchise history. Jason Garrett spent those same years mostly waiting for his chance behind him, while learning how an NFL offense worked from inside the quarterback room.

Garrett had more to do than hold a clipboard on game day. He also wore the headset, took plays from offensive coordinator Ernie Zampese and passed them along to Aikman.

Jason Garrett remembers being stuck between Troy Aikman and Ernie Zampese

Garrett told The Dan Patrick Show that the arrangement could become awkward on third down. If Aikman disliked a play call and Dallas failed to convert, the Hall of Fame quarterback would sometimes direct his frustration at Garrett.

"He'd come over to me, and he would rip me up and down as if I made the call," Garrett said .

Aikman would then send Garrett back to Zampese with the complaint. "Then he'd say, 'You tell that guy upstairs,'" Garrett recalled.

That put Garrett in the middle. Zampese had called the play, Aikman had rejected it and Garrett had to deliver the quarterback's response to the coaching staff. Garrett even recalled trying to soften the message: "Hey, Ernie, I'm not sure he really likes it. That's what you're going to tell him," he recalled.

Troy Aikman's standards were high in Dallas Cowboys

The story reflects Aikman's standing in Dallas during those years. He led the Cowboys to three Super Bowl titles in the 1990s and remained the starting quarterback throughout Garrett's time with the team. Garrett spent seven seasons in Dallas from 1993 through 1999 but made only nine starts.

Zampese also played an important role in the offense. He served as Dallas' offensive coordinator from 1994 through 1997, including the 1995 season when the Cowboys won Super Bowl XXX. That left Garrett in an unusual position, close enough to hear Aikman's complaints but with no control over the play calls that caused them.

Garrett was caught between two of the most influential people on the offense while holding little power himself. He later spent nine seasons as the Cowboys' head coach, but his role during the Aikman years was much simpler. He was the backup quarterback who sometimes took the blame for a call he never made.

articles.title: Joel Klatt: Moving On From Lincoln Riley Could Cost USC $100-120 Million
articles.summary: How much would it actually cost USC to move on from head coach Lincoln Riley? Joel Klatt explains why it would be a LOT more than $70 million.
articles.body: Lincoln Riley is feeling the heat at USC. The Trojans had a golden opportunity last week to pick up a statement win against Big Ten foe Oregon. Instead, they fell flat in a 41-27 loss to the Ducks, adding another disappointing chapter to Riley’s tenure and fueling calls from USC fans for a change. So, where does USC go from here? The "Big Noon Kickoff" crew tackled that question Saturday, and former USC quarterback and Heisman winner Matt Leinart didn't mince words when describing the current state of the program. "They’re stuck in the mud with nowhere to go," Leinart said. FOX Sports’ Joel Klatt took the conversation a step further, pointing to what he believes is a broader frustration that goes beyond wins and losses. "These fans are frustrated with the culture," Klatt said. Klatt pointed to the targeting penalty on USC safety Desman Stephens II during last week’s loss to Oregon. After Stephens’ hit knocked Oregon quarterback Dante Moore out of the game, Stephens was seen celebrating and exchanging high-fives with teammates while Moore was being attended to by Oregon’s medical staff. "They’re frustrated with Desman Stephens, and there was nobody that walked up to him and said, ‘Hey, we’re not going to do that anymore,’" Klatt said. There has been plenty of discussion about whether USC could move on from Riley despite the massive buyout that would come with doing so. "I’m just going to throw up a bit of a caution flag," Klatt said. "There are a lot of people talking about, ‘We need to replace Lincoln Riley.’ It’s not just the $70 million that you’re going to have to spend to buy out Lincoln Riley. You’re going to have to buy out the staff. You’re going to have to buy out the next coach from his contract. Plus, you’re going to have to build an elite roster. "It’s really like $100 to $120 million that you’ll have to spend to make a change." Klatt believes USC should look no further than Penn State, which moved on from James Franklin last season after coming within reach of the College Football Playoff National Championship the previous season. "Look at what happened last night," Klatt said, referencing Penn State's 34-13 loss to Northwestern. "There was a program that was this close to the mountaintop, a national finalist, lost a couple games that they thought they should win, and now they just got their head kicked in by Northwestern at Ryan Field all because they felt they needed to make a change." The Trojans entered the season with the nation’s No. 1-ranked recruiting class, but a coaching change could put that talented group at risk. "All the best coaches in the nation are praying that USC makes a change," Klatt said. "Because all the best coaches — Dan Lanning, Ryan Day, Kirby Smart, Lane Kiffin — all of their GMs will be parked in Los Angeles looking at [USC’s young players]." Klatt specifically mentioned freshmen Luke Wafle, Kaden Dixon-Wyatt, Trent Mosley and tight end Mark Bowman as players opposing programs could target if USC were to undergo a coaching change. "I think they have one of the elite freshman classes in all of college football," Klatt said. Starting over would come with an enormous price tag for the Trojans — financially and potentially on the roster. So would making a change actually put USC in a better position? "When I look at a change," Klatt said, "I don’t think it actually makes them better going forward." articles.title: Shenzhen Open: Wu Yize beats Judd Trump to set up final against Yuan Sijun
articles.summary: Chinese world champion Wu Yize wins six consecutive frames to beat Judd Trump 6-1 at the Shenzhen Open and set up a final against countryman Yuan Sijun.
articles.body:
Reigning world champion Wu Yize won six consecutive frames to beat Judd Trump 6-1 in the Shenzhen Open semi-finals.

Wu, who will leapfrog Trump in the rankings and move second in the world after the final, bounced back in dramatic fashion after losing the opening frame to set up an all-Chinese final against Yuan Sijun at the Bao'an Sports Centre on Sunday.

Yuan, 26, endured a much more difficult route to his maiden ranking final, battling through 6-5 against Englishman Jimmy Robertson.

World number two Trump, who won the Shanghai Masters in August, had gone into the Shenzhen semi-final in fine form after beating Mark Selby 5-0 in the last eight.

But after clinching the opening frame with a break of 77, the 2019 world champion handed the initiative to his opponent with a string of errors.

Wu, 22, capitalised to avenge a defeat by Trump at the last-four stage in Shanghai earlier this year, making three breaks of 50 or more in a scrappy encounter before clinching victory with a break of 110.

"When I was preparing for the evening match, I saw that Yuan had shed some tears," Wu told World Snooker Tour.

"I believe it is his first ranking final. Hopefully, we can put on a great match for everyone. Of course, I hope I can take the trophy home, but we will both give it everything we have."

An emotional Yuan found it much more difficult to get over the winning line, with the lead continually changing hands throughout the best-of-11 encounter before his opponent forced a deciding frame that took 50 minutes to complete and saw a total of 177 points scored.

Robertson put Yuan in a difficult snooker on the final red and clawed back 41 penalty points before himself being put in a snooker, with Yuan finally clearing to the pink to earn his place in the final of the inaugural event.

"I feel that my first ranking final has come a little bit late," said Yuan, who started the tournament as the world number 33 but would move to the cusp of the top 16 with victory on Sunday.

"Since the pandemic in 2020, the years in between have been quite difficult, and I feel it hasn't been easy. So after all these years, I just hope I can give myself something to show for it."

articles.title: Oregon Coach Dan Lanning Gives Positive Dante Moore Injury Update
articles.summary: Oregon head coach Dan Lanning provided a positive update on QB Dante Moore, who suffered a concussion against USC.
articles.body: Dante Moore appears to be on the right track. The Oregon quarterback, who suffered a concussion in last week’s win over USC, is recovering and appears to be trending in the right direction, according to head coach Dan Lanning. Lanning provided an update on Moore’s health Saturday on "Big Noon Kickoff," saying the senior quarterback "is going to be OK" while emphasizing that Oregon will take an abundance of caution with his recovery. "It's looking like he's going to be OK," Lanning said about Moore. "I'm grateful that God has his hand over him and in recovery mode right now. We'll just continue to proceed with an abundance of caution to make sure that he's ready to go whenever he's able to step back out there for us." With 10:05 remaining in the second quarter of Oregon's 41-27 win over USC last Saturday, Moore attempted to slide but was struck in the head by linebacker Desman Stephens II. Following the hit, the two sides had to be separated, with Lanning incensed at the hit. Stephens was suspended by USC for its Week 5 home tilt against Washington. Dylan Raiola, who started at quarterback for Nebraska from 2024-25, stepped in for Moore and was sensational. He completed 19 of 25 passes for 289 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions, posting a 199.5 passer rating in the Ducks' win over USC. The week before, Raiola completed all 11 of his passes for 124 yards and three touchdowns against Portland State. "I'm just so proud of him," Lanning said of Raiola. "You talk about owning a role and not waiting for your opportunity but preparing for your opportunity, and Dylan's a guy that prepared for his opportunity." Oregon improved to 3-1 after its Week 4 win over USC, moving up to No. 15 in the AP Top 25 Poll. The Ducks began the season ranked No. 2, but fell to No. 6 after squeaking out a home win over Boise State before dropping to No. 21 following an upset loss at Oklahoma State. The Ducks have a bye in Week 5, followed by a ranked matchup at home against No. 23-ranked UCLA on Oct. 10.

articles.title: Screensaver turns real: Aman Sehrawat’s gold on phone now around his neck
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: For months, Aman Sehrawat had carried a picture of the Asian Games gold medal on his phone.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: For months, Aman Sehrawat had carried a picture of the Asian Games gold medal on his phone. It was more than a wallpaper; it was a daily reminder of the colour he wanted after returning from Hangzhou with bronze. On Saturday, after beating North Korea’s reigning world champion Han Chong Song 11-7 in the 57kg final, Sehrawat looked at the real medal, bit it, and allowed himself a moment of disbelief. The picture had become reality.The road to it had not been smooth. A cut beneath his left eye left him bruised during the bout, but not distracted. Han surged back from 1-6 to lead 7-6, yet Sehrawat answered with two takedowns, regained control and closed out the comeback. Earlier, he had beaten Japan’s Yamato Ogawa 20-9, Kazakhstan’s Nurdanat Aitanov 12-1 and Tajikistan’s Aiaal Belolyubskii 14-8.The gold also carries a difficult lesson. Last year, Sehrawat was eliminated from the World Championships after weighing 1.7kg over the 57kg limit, which led to a one-year suspension from the Wrestling Federation of India (WFI). The ban was later lifted after he apologised. He competed at 61kg in the Zagreb Open and Asian Championships, taking silver at both, before returning to 57kg and winning the Budapest Ranking Series event ahead of the Games.Weight had become a difficult proportion to manage, but that discipline made Saturday sweeter. Sehrawat, now 23, is already a U-23 world champion, a Paris Olympic bronze medallist and a Hangzhou bronze medallist. Now he has added the continental crown and upgraded his Asian Games colour from bronze to gold.Sehrawat’s wrestling journey began in far darker circumstances. He lost his mother at 10 and his father a year later, leaving him orphaned at 11. His maternal uncles stepped in, brought him to Delhi’s Chhatrasal Stadium and set him on a path from grief to purpose. Under coach Lalit Kumar, the boy from Haryana became a solid wrestler with a force to reckon with.India’s remarkable wrestling campaign at the ongoing edition became even sweeter, and historic as well, after Antim Panghal’s silver in women's 53kg and Deepak Punia’s bronze in men's 97kg took the nation's tally to six wrestling medals — two gold, two silver and two bronze. It was the country’s best Asian Games haul in 64 years. The last time India collected more was Jakarta in 1962, with 12 medals.Antim, a Hangzhou bronze medallist, reached the final of her weight division hoping to become only the second Indian woman after Vinesh Phogat to win Asian Games wrestling gold. Japan’s Moe Kiyooka, however, proved too sharp, controlling the contest and winning 9-1. Antim’s silver still underlined a strong campaign, though gold remained beyond reach.Punia added bronze after edging Mongolia’s Gankhuyag Ganbaatar 2-1 in the medal-deciding repechage bout. He had beaten China’s Zhou Junpeng 12-2 before a quarterfinal walkover, then lost an 8-9 semifinal to Uzbekistan’s Sherzod Poyonov. He recovered to finish on the podium.For Indian wrestling, Nagoya ended with an impressive haul. articles.title: Yankees Make 2026 ALDS Roster Decision On Aaron Judge
articles.summary: Yankees captain Aaron Judge was left off the roster for New York’s AL Division Series against the Tampa Bay Rays.
articles.body: Yankees captain Aaron Judge was left off the roster for New York's AL Division Series against the Tampa Bay Rays while he tries to work his way back from a calf injury. A three-time AL MVP, Judge hasn’t played since Sept. 16. Giancarlo Stanton, who hasn’t played since April 24 because of strained calf muscles in both legs, remained on the 26-man roster for the best-of-five series starting Saturday. Stanton was active for the Wild Card Series sweep of the Boston Red Sox but didn’t get in the games, which both turned into blowouts. Judge was sidelined by a fractured rib from May 31 to Sept. 8 and played in just seven games before straining his right calf. He was limited to 66 games this season and hit .241 with 18 homers, 41 RBIs and an .871 OPS, including .174 with one homer and three RBIs in September. Left-hander Ryan Weathers, sidelined with a left forearm flexor strain since Aug. 22, was added to the roster as an 11th pitcher. Utilityman Amed Rosario was dropped. He had two plate appearances in the Wild Card Series with a walk and a strikeout. Tampa Bay's 12 pitchers included right-hander Cole Susler and left-hander Steven Matz over right-handers Brody Hopkins, Casey Legumina and Manuel Rodriguez. Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: Portugal vs Norway: UEFA Nations League – Ronaldo latest, Haaland, teams
articles.summary: Nations League title holders Portugal hosts Erling Haaland’s Norway, days after Cristiano Ronaldo’s exit from the camp.
articles.body:
Who : Portugal vs Norway What : UEFA Nations League 2026-27 , Group A4 match Where : Estadio do Dragao, Porto, Portugal When : Sunday, October 4, at 8:45pm local time (18:45 GMT) How to follow: Al Jazeera Sport will bring you all the build-up and live updates from 15:45 GMT.

For the second time in a week, Portugal and Norway clash in the UEFA Nations League. But this time, things are not quite the same in the Selecao camp.

Sunday’s fixture in Porto will see the Nations League title holders play without their talisman, Cristiano Ronaldo, after the 41-year-old abruptly left their camp , raising questions about his international future.

Ronaldo’s dramatic exit and apparent rift with new coach Jorge Jesus have dominated headlines worldwide. Portuguese players have largely blocked the outside noise, however, maintaining a perfect record at the tournament where they are chasing a record-extending third crown.

Opponents Norway have won just one match, despite boasting a talented side that defied expectations with a historic quarterfinal finish at this year’s FIFA World Cup .

However, their striker Erling Haaland – one of Europe’s most lethal players – poses enough danger to put Portugal under pressure ahead of this weekend’s thrilling encounter.

The UEFA Nations League was founded in 2018 to reduce the number of meaningless friendlies and give nations competitive matches against top-ranked teams.

In this competition, countries from across Europe participate in a league structure which features promotion and relegation.

What is the latest news on Cristiano Ronaldo?

Ronaldo left the squad late on Wednesday, shortly after a news conference in which coach Jesus confirmed the five-time Ballon d’Or winner would be left out of his starting line-up for a second consecutive Nations League game.

The 41-year-old’s decision to walk out came as a shock as he had been due to train with his teammates at the Parken Stadium in Copenhagen.

Portugal’s leading scorer with 146 goals had already spent the entirety of last weekend’s 2-1 Nations League win in Norway on the bench, having captained the side in the 1-0 home victory over Wales last Thursday.

He appeared to indicate that the reasons behind Jesus’s decision ran deeper and hinted at a departure from the national team he has graced for more than two decades.

“In due course, I will tell the truth to all the Portuguese people about my reasons for leaving the national team, to which I have always been dedicated,” Ronaldo said in a cryptic Instagram post, announcing his sudden exit from the camp.

Spanish sports daily Marca said that Jesus and Portuguese federation president Pedro Proenca followed Ronaldo to Copenhagen airport in an attempt to persuade him to stay with the squad, before the player boarded his private jet.

Jesus insisted earlier on Wednesday that there was no rift between them, although the 72-year-old, who was appointed in July, acknowledged that his captain was disappointed to remain on the bench against Norway.

How have Portugal and Norway played in the Nations League?

Portugal are on top of Group A4 on nine points, with three wins out of three. They started their campaign with a 1-0 home win over Wales, before adding a 2-1 victory over Norway in Oslo. In the last match, they thrashed Denmark 4-2 in Copenhagen.

Norway are second-bottom in the group, with only three points. They started their campaign with a 3-2 home win over fellow Scandinavians Denmark but suffered identical 2-1 defeats at home to Portugal and to Wales in Cardiff.

They met in matchday two of this year’s Nations League, with Portugal beating Norway 2-1 in Oslo.

Joao Felix and Goncalo Ramos scored for Portugal, while Haaland struck the consolation goal for Norway.

Joao Felix and Goncalo Ramos (Portugal): Al Nassr forward Felix has emerged as the reliable scorer in the Portugal setup, finding the net in each of the three games this term. Meanwhile, Ramos, playing in place of Ronaldo, has made up for CR7’s absence with goals in the last two matches.

Erling Haaland and Oscar Bobb (Norway) : All of Norway’s goals in the ongoing competition have come through Haaland (three) and Bobb (two). While their partnership proved successful in the opening match, their goals were not enough in the following matches, as the Norwegians suffered back-to-back defeats. Norwegians will demand better from Haaland, especially after the Manchester City talisman’s incredible start to the club season that features seven goals in as many games.

Winger Francisco Conceicao is doubtful for the game due to a thigh injury.

Wing-back Julian Ryerson is doubtful with a muscle injury, while centre-back Torbjorn Heggem is suspended.

articles.title: Fernandes hails Ronaldo and calls for Portugal unity ahead of Norway game
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo withdrew from the Portugal squad, but Bruno Fernandes says forward remains team’s ‘greatest symbol’.
articles.body:
Portugal playmaker Bruno Fernandes said Cristiano Ronaldo remains the country’s greatest footballing icon despite walking out on the squad this week after finding out he would not start a match.

The 41-year-old superstar said on Wednesday that he had left the team after coach Jorge Jesus said he would not start against Denmark in the Nations League, a match Portugal won 4-2 without him.

The former Real Madrid and Manchester United attacker’s future with the national team, for whom he is the leading goalscorer and most capped player, is in doubt after his walkout.

“Regarding Cristiano, I had a conversation with him, and what I told him, and what I repeat here, is this – the most important thing is that, regardless of what happens, Cristiano Ronaldo will never cease to be the greatest symbol of our national team, of our football, and of the country, for what he has done not only in Portugal but throughout the world,” Fernandes told reporters on Saturday.

Manchester United midfielder Fernandes called for unity after a tumultuous few days in which Portugal fans’ opinions have been split over Ronaldo’s decision.

“He has a reserved place not only among the best of all time, but also in the hearts of all Portuguese people and the most important thing is that we stop dividing things,” said Fernandes.

“There are no divisions in the national team, it is one and will remain so, despite any noise that may come from outside…

“We are outside of this controversy, but what I ask is that the country does not divide itself, does not make choices, that it respects all sides, but, at the same time, Cris is and will be the biggest icon of our national team, he deserves everyone’s respect, regardless of who likes him more or (who likes him) less.”

Portugal beat Norway and Denmark away from home without Ronaldo starting and face Norway again on Sunday.

Coach Jesus said Ronaldo was a “symbol of Portugal” and said there would be time to speak about him after Sunday’s game in Porto.

“I’m going to focus on the team, on the opponent which is Norway, one of the five best teams in Europe. That’s the problem right now,” said the 72-year-old coach.

articles.title: Craziest upset of the college football season happened on Friday night while everyone was asleep
articles.summary: Joshua Wood's last-second touchdown stunned undefeated Montana State inside the Kibbie Dome, ending the FCS national champion's 19-game winning streak.
articles.body: Friday nights in the fall are normally reserved for high school football, but the college game had some pretty entertaining matchups that served as an appetizer for an absolutely loaded Saturday slate. Northwestern proved their close loss to Indiana was not a fluke, as they bludgeoned Penn State at home to give the new coaching staff in Happy Valley some more tough questions that need answering. There was also Virginia Tech and Pitt's thrilling (and controversial) ending in the battle of "why aren't we ranked in the AP Poll" occupying the primetime slot. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! But, the most entertaining and consequential ending of the night happened in a small town in Idaho while the rest of the college football watching world was likely asleep. Montana State waltzed into the Kibbie Dome in Moscow, Idaho, expecting to take care of business against a winless Vandals team. Instead, the Bobcats bit off a bit more than they could chew. Let's start with the actual ending of the game on the field. Idaho had the ball at midfield trailing 34-27 with eight seconds left and no timeouts - that's an important detail. As Vandals quarterback Joshua Wood completed a pass for a first down, the clock ticked closer to zero. CLOCK CONTROVERSY: NCAA SAYS OFFICIALS BOTCHED REPLAY PROTOCOL IN MICHIGAN'S WIN OVER WESTERN MICHIGAN That is, until Montana State coach Brent Vigen inexplicably called a timeout, essentially gifting the Vandals one last play. That strategy backfired horrifically, as Wood fired a pass to wide receiver Ryan Jezioro smack dab in the middle of the endzone. An extra point would have tied the game and sent it to overtime, but Idaho said "no thank you," and ran a QB draw to cap off a 14-point fourth quarter comeback with an outright win in regulation. Pretty insane, right? COLLEGE FOOTBALL WEEK 4 CONTENDERS, PRETENDERS: TEXAS SURVIVES, MICHIGAN'S KARMA AND COACHES ARE SWEATING It gets even crazier when you consider that the Vandals were winless this season while the Bobcats were undefeated and the number one team in FCS. Oh, and by the way, Montana State is the reigning FCS national champion and carried a 19-game winning streak into the Kibbie Dome on Friday night. Talk about David vs. Goliath! There might have been some extra motivation in this one too, as the Bobcats knocked Idaho out of the FCS Playoffs in 2024. High level, Power 4 college football is awesome, there's no question about it, but if you can't appreciate a good FCS matchup like this, then you don't actually love college football. Who knows what could happen to games like this if the highest level of the sport continues down the path it's on, but for now, I'm going to keep enjoying some damn good football. articles.title: Paula y Bea vuelven a una final y las número uno caen eliminadas
articles.standfirst: La malagueña y la extremeña pelearán por el título en el Rotterdam P2 ante Ari Sánchez y Andrea Ustero, que superaron en semifinales a Gemma Triay y Delfi Brea
articles.summary: La malagueña y la extremeña pelearán por el título en el Rotterdam P2 ante Ari Sánchez y Andrea Ustero, que superaron en semifinales a Gemma Triay y Delfi Brea
articles.body: El circuito femenino afronta el tramo decisivo de la temporada inmerso en una notable igualdad en la zona alta de la tabla. En las semifinales del CUPRA Rotterdam Premier Padel P2, Bea González y Paula Josemaría reencontraron su mejor versión para certificar su presencia en la gran final de este domingo. Enfrente no estarán las número uno del ranking FIP, Gemma Triay y Delfi Brea, quienes cayeron superadas ante unas inspiradas Ari Sánchez y Andrea Ustero. Josemaría y González no atravesaban su periodo más regular de la campaña. Tras caer en la ronda de cuartos de final en el Major de París y ceder opciones en la pelea por el liderato de la tabla, la extremeña y la malagueña afrontaban un choque exigente en el recinto Ahoy ante Claudia Fernández y Martina Calvo, una de las duplas más en forma del circuito tras sus recientes finales en Madrid y la capital francesa. Sin embargo, el guion sobre la moqueta neerlandesa favoreció desde el inicio a las cabezas de serie número dos. Moviendo la bola con altura y recuperando la agresividad en la red, la 'Perla' y 'Dinamita' dominaron la primera manga para adjudicársela por 6-3. En el segundo parcial, Fernández y Calvo trataron de igualar la contienda desde el volumen de juego, pero la firmeza de Josemaría en la derecha y el despliegue físico de González en el remate decantaron los momentos clave. El 6-4 definitivo sella el regreso de la pareja a una final cuatro meses después de su última aparición en el partido por el título, abriendo una oportunidad para sumar un nuevo trofeo a su casillero. En la segunda semifinal del cuadro femenino, Ari Sánchez y Andrea Ustero prolongaron las buenas sensaciones mostradas tras proclamarse campeonas en la pista Philippe Chatrier hace dos semanas. La dupla catalana se vio las caras con Gemma Triay y Delfi Brea, quienes venían de firmar una trayectoria sólida en las rondas previas. Pese a que el desarrollo de los puntos presentó fases de intercambio prolongado, la efectividad en las bolas de break marcó la diferencia a favor de la tercera pareja del ranking. Sánchez aportó la pausa táctica en la construcción del punto, mientras que Ustero volvió a exhibir su pegada zurda para desequilibrar la defensa de las de Seba Nerone. Un rotundo 6-2 en el primer set inclinó la balanza. En la segunda manga, Triay y Brea buscaron variar la dinámica del encuentro e intentaron una reacción para acortar distancias en el marcador. No obstante, la solidez defensiva de la reusense y la agresividad en el juego aéreo de la barcelonesa frenaron el empuje de las número uno, cerrando el choque con un nuevo 6-2 que confirma la segunda final consecutiva para Sánchez y Ustero. La moqueta del Ahoy Rotterdam acogerá este domingo un duelo directo por el título entre Paula Josemaría y Bea González frente a Ari Sánchez y Andrea Ustero, con puntos clave en juego para la Race de la temporada 2026.

articles.title: Jon Sanz y Franco Stupaczuk confirman su redención en Rotterdam
articles.standfirst: El navarro y el chaqueño superaron con solvencia a Mike Yanguas y Coki Nieto para citarse con Arturo Coello y Agustín Tapia en la pelea por el título del P2 neerlandés
articles.summary: El navarro y el chaqueño superaron con solvencia a Mike Yanguas y Coki Nieto para citarse con Arturo Coello y Agustín Tapia en la pelea por el título del P2 neerlandés
articles.body: El deporte acostumbra a ofrecer giros de guion inesperados, y la trayectoria de Jon Sanz y Franco Stupaczuk en este CUPRA Rotterdam Premier Padel P2 es el mejor reflejo de ello. Tras haber unido sus caminos en busca de sensaciones y haber afrontado un inicio de proyecto con altibajos, el zurdo de Pamplona y el jugador chaqueño han confirmado su mejoría colectiva en tierras neerlandesas. Tras eliminar a Ale Galán y Fede Chingotto en cuartos de final, la pareja número cinco del torneo certificó su pase a la gran final del domingo al imponerse a Mike Yanguas y Coki Nieto por 6-0 y 6-4. En el primer parcial de las semifinales, Sanz y Stupaczuk desplegaron un volumen de juego incisivo que desarmó el esquema táctico de sus oponentes. La firmeza de Sanz en la construcción de los puntos, sumada a la movilidad y agresividad de Stupaczuk en la red, se tradujo en un contundente 6-0 en la primera manga sobre la moqueta del recinto Ahoy. En el segundo set, Yanguas y Nieto ajustaron su posicionamiento en pista y elevaron el nivel defensivo para equilibrar los intercambios. No obstante, Sanz y Stupaczuk mantuvieron la compostura en los momentos decisivos del parcial. Un quiebre en el tramo final decantó la balanza para sellar el definitivo 6-4, un resultado que clasifica por primera vez a la dupla hispano-argentina para la final de un torneo de categoría Premier Padel. Además del impacto deportivo, el triunfo tiene consecuencias directas en la clasificación FIP. Con este resultado, Sanz y Stupaczuk aseguran matemáticamente el regreso a la cuarta posición del ranking mundial de cara a los próximos torneos en Düsseldorf y Milán, un estatus clave que les permitirá figurar entre los cuatro primeros cabezas de serie del cuadro. En el duelo decisivo por el título, los número cinco (a partir del lunes, cuatro) se medirán a las primeras raquetas del ranking, Arturo Coello y Agustín Tapia. La dupla dirigida por Gustavo Pratto volvió a sobreponerse a un encuentro exigente tras superar en tres sets a Momo González y Lucas Campagnolo. Los 'Golden Boys' arrancaron el choque con contundencia, adjudicándose el primer parcial por 6-1 gracias a la velocidad que imprimieron al juego aéreo. Sin embargo, González y Campagnolo reaccionaron en la segunda manga, aprovechando una fase de imprecisiones de los líderes del ranking para igualar la contienda con un 6-3. En el set definitivo, Coello y Tapia recuperaron la solvencia desde el servicio y el resto, abrochando el pase a la final con un nuevo 6-1. El choque de este domingo en el Ahoy Rotterdam pondrá en juego el trofeo del P2 neerlandés, con Coello y Tapia buscando consolidar su ventaja en el liderato de la tabla y Sanz y Stupaczuk en persecución de su primer título conjunto del curso.

articles.title: Lamine Yamal Scores Golazo And Spain's Unbeaten Streak Continues
articles.summary: Lamine Yamal has kept up his run of early goals as Spain are now riding a 41-game unbeaten streak.
articles.body: Lamine Yamal kept up his run of early goals in the Nations League when he put Spain ahead with a superb sixth-minute goal against Czechia on Saturday. Spain, winners of this summer's World Cup, have now gone 41 matches without a loss. Spain coach Luis de la Fuente shook his head in admiration and disbelief as Yamal cut inside down the right and unleashed a powerful curling shot with his left foot into the top left corner. Goalkeeper Antonín Kinský could not even get near the ball. This trademark Yamal strike followed the 19-year-old star's second-minute goals against Croatia in a 4-1 win on Tuesday and away to England in a 3-2 victory on Sept. 26. The Ballon d'Or contender has also been in outstanding form for defending La Liga champion Barcelona this season. Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: England Puts 7 Goals Past Croatia As Kane, Saka, Bellingham All Shine
articles.summary: Harry Kane and Bukayo Saka have scored two each as England crushed Croatia 7-0 in UEFA Nations League action.
articles.body: Harry Kane and Bukayo Saka scored two each as ruthless England crushed Croatia 7-0 away in the Nations League on Saturday. Ballon d’Or contender Kane extended his national record to 89 international goals. Left winger Anthony Gordon set up Jude Bellingham and grabbed one for himself. Substitute Morgan Rogers completed the rout in Rijeka. "It was very impressive, and we created so many chances. In the first 40 minutes we were so fluid right from the start. It just never stopped," England coach Thomas Tuchel said. "We just kept the pace up and played through the gaps. We were very, very clinical." Later in other League A play, World Cup champion Spain hosted Czechia in Oviedo and looked to make it 40 straight games unbeaten. Switzerland faced Slovenia and Scotland went to North Macedonia in League B matches. England cruises Kane put England ahead in the eighth minute, controlling a pass from Bellingham with the outside of his right foot and then curling the ball into the top left corner. Bellingham poked in Gordon's cross midway through the first half. Gordon stooped to head in Jarell Quansah's right-wing cross and Saka side-footed in England's fourth approaching halftime. After the break, Croatia's defense was sliced open again on a quick break and Elliot Anderson curled in a cross from the right and Kane slid in at the back post for a poacher's finish. "We’re at our best when we’re free, when we’re physically just overpowering," Kane said. "They couldn’t live with our pace, our movement, our runs." More bad defending saw Croatia unable to clear the ball and it ended up at the feet of Kane, who gifted Saka his second in the 68th. Rogers controlled Bellingham’s pass with his heel and slotted in from an angle. The result eclipsed England’s previous highest score against Croatia, 5-1 in World Cup qualifying in 2009 at Wembley. Tuchel’s England moved onto six points from three games. Bad start for Bilić It was another tough match for Croatia coach Slaven Bilić following Tuesday's 4-1 loss in Spain. His side has conceded 12 goals in three matches. Luka Modric started the game in Rijeka but the 41-year-old looked frustrated by his team's sloppy performance.

articles.title: 3 free agent cornerbacks Steelers should sign after Joey Porter Jr trade
articles.summary: Three veteran cornerbacks Pittsburgh should target after poor performance vs. Browns.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers' secondary was seen as a very deep unit heading into the season. However, following the Joey Porter Jr trade and an ankle injury to Jamel Dean, the Steelers suddenly have a need at cornerback after Daylen Everette was torched on Thursday.

A trade for a notable name would be nice, but the likelier outcome is a free agent signing. There are multiple notable names available that would make sense, and here are a few of my favorites.

Kelly is already an NFL journeyman just three years into his career. After spending 2023 with three teams, Kelly spent 2024 and 2025 with the Las Vegas Raiders under defensive coordinator Patrick Graham, and had a solid 2025 season that saw him pick off three passes in 13 games. At minimum, he knows the defense and would be better than Everette was against Cleveland. He did suffer a season-ending knee injury last December, which is a large reason he is still available.

Lattimore didn't have the best run with the Washington Commanders, but he was largely solid in zone coverage last season. He broke up three passes and allowed less than a yard per coverage snap when the Commanders were in zone, per Sumer Sports. The only pushback here would be Lattimore's age, as he is 30 years old.

Again, White is on the older side at 31 years of age. But like Lattimore, he was good in zone looks last year. Anytime you see these former high-end corners age, they usually are still good in zone looks due to their high football IQs. In 275 coverage snaps, White allowed 16 receptions as the nearest defender and 0.64 yards per coverage snap. with six pass breakups and an interception.

articles.title: Hawks Defense And Rookie Depth Define First Week Of Camp
articles.summary: The Atlanta Hawks finished camp with a clear identity. See how new veterans and rookies aim to fix the guard depth and build a top-tier defense.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Hawks left Nashville with a plan. They want to be a tough, physical team that grinds opponents down. This is a big change from years past. The team traded away their biggest star, Trae Young, to Washington. Now, Jalen Johnson leads the charge as the main franchise player. The goal is simple: make the playoffs and actually win a series. They did not make huge roster swaps this summer. Instead, they added veteran depth and young rookies. According to Sports Illustrated , the team hopes these new pieces will be the difference maker. The starting lineup looks set. CJ McCollum, Dyson Daniels, Nickeil Alexander-Walker, Jalen Johnson, and Onyeka Okongwu are the core. But the bench needs to step up. In the last playoff loss to the Knicks, the Hawks had no one to turn to except Jonathan Kuminga. That cannot happen again.

Head coach Quin Snyder wants a specific feel on the court. He spoke about building a new identity during the first week of practice. "But fundamentally, we took some steps to really carve out and begin to build an identity," Snyder said. The team is trying to be defensive-minded. They added Lu Dort and Aaron Wiggins for that exact reason. These players know how to stop the other team from scoring easy points. The East is getting harder, but the Hawks believe they can keep up. Their new depth and chemistry might be the key to success.

Defense is the priority right now. Almost any opponent can be shut down by a group of Hawks players. Dyson Daniels, Lu Dort, Nickeil Alexander-Walker, and Onyeka Okongwu form a scary wall. Per Yahoo Sports , Atlanta finished in the top 10 for defensive rating last season. That was the first time they did that since the 2016-17 season. For years before that, they were in the bottom 10. The team is going all-in on this style without Trae Young. Dyson Daniels has Lu Dort adding more wing defense nearby. The coach noted that defense usually comes before offense. "Yeah, I think particularly early in the year, really the whole year, but your defense is usually ahead of your offense," Snyder explained. This is okay as long as the defense is good. The team can lean on their defense while the offense learns to work together. Communication is a huge part of this. Snyder wants to see that early focus to make the team tough to beat night after night.

Jalen Johnson has a new job. He is helping the rookies learn the ropes. This is his first season as the clear leader. He needs to guide the younger players through the new system. The team moved Zaccharie Risacher to Dallas after just two years. That was a tough decision for a number one pick. But it signaled that the team is moving forward with a different vision. The stats show Risacher did better with Trae Young, but the fit was not right. Now, the Hawks must prove they can win without that specific playmaker. The defense will have to carry the load early on.

There is a worry about the guard spot. The starting trio of McCollum, Alexander-Walker, and Daniels is solid. But the bench looks thin. The Hawks waived Devin Carter and traded Ryan Nembhard. They drafted Kingston Flemings, but he is a rookie. Two-way players like RayJ Davis and Keshon Gilbert were great in the G League. However, asking them to play big minutes in the NBA might be a stretch. Two-way players cannot play in the playoffs anyway. Aaron Wiggins might need to take on more responsibility. He used to just hit open threes and play defense with Oklahoma City. Now, he might have to handle the ball more. If Wiggins cannot fill that role, the pressure on rookie Flemings will be huge. Rookies often struggle with such big tasks.

Hawks President of Basketball Operations Onsi Saleh thinks the team is fine. He told reporters he feels confident in the depth. "Yeah, like we're really excited about our guards. We feel like we're pretty deep at that position in a lot of ways," Saleh said. He listed CJ, Nickeil, Dyson, and Kingston as key players. He also noted that Jalen Johnson handles the ball often too. The talent is there. The opportunity is there. But the risk is real. If the guards do not click, the team could struggle. The first preseason game against the Memphis Grizzlies will show if the guards can hold their own. The Hawks have a chance to be a contender, but they must solve this depth puzzle first.

articles.title: Tennessee football QB George MacIntyre replaces Faizon Brandon vs Auburn
articles.summary: Tennessee backup quarterback George MacIntyre replaced freshman starter Faizon Brandon in the second quarter against Auburn on Oct. 3.
articles.body:
Tennessee backup quarterback George MacIntyre replaced freshman starter Faizon Brandon in the second quarter against Auburn on Oct. 3.

"Faizon just wasn't operating. He wasn't feeling 100%," coach Josh Heupel told ESPN at halftime.

UT trailed 7-3 with 3:42 remaining in the second quarter when it swapped quarterbacks. MacIntyre finished the half 5-of-5 for 38 yards in relief.

The Vols had a terrible offensive start with Brandon and a makeshift offensive line.

Brandon was 3-of-8 passing for no yards and one interception. He also had four rushing attempts for minus-9 yards. That included sacks on back-to-back plays and a 12-yard loss on a lateral when he was hit attempting the pass.

Brandon's interception came deep in UT territory and gave Auburn's its first points of the game.

MacIntyre is a sophomore and former Brentwood Academy standout. He entered the game with 62 yards passing and one TD in three games as a backup this season.
