articles.title: #1 UNC Women’s Soccer extends its win streak to 8 with a win over #12 Notre Dame
articles.summary: The Tar Heels are on a roll.
articles.body:
After a disappointing season last year, Damon Nahas and UNC women's soccer started this year on a tear, right up until they dropped a home nonconference game , a rarity for this program, against Michigan State in their 4th game of the season. Michigan State was ranked 5th in the country and is now ranked 2nd, so that wasn't a bad loss whatsoever, but it still seems to have galvanized the Heels — since then, they've won 8 straight games, including 3 against ranked conference opponents. The latest in that stretch happened on Friday night with an absolute drubbing of #12 Notre Dame, ending in a 4-1 UNC win.

The game felt, for much of the first half, even more lopsided than that final score. The Heels dominated possession in the opening minutes, coming close to converting a corner kick in the first six minutes and eventually putting one on the board courtesy of Bella Devey, who converted from a sharp angle after a feed from Lilliah Blum. Devey picked up a brace a few minutes later, after Amari Manning earned a penalty that Devey roofed to make it 2-0 17 minutes in. It was Devey's 4th two-goal game of the season, and the penalty gave her 14 goals on the year — a mark that I believe is 2nd in the country (the NCAA hasn't updated their stats yet. She's definitely top-5). Notre Dame cut the lead in half with a nice set piece goal, but that didn't stop the Heels' onslaught. Manning got the ball down the left flank off a deep service and crossed the ball past two defenders to find Blum, who got herself a tap-in goal via Manning's team-leading 5th assist of the season.

The Heels stayed on the gas in the second half. It didn't lead to as many goals as in the first, but they kept the Irish off the ball and created a ton of opportunities while snuffing out any counters that Notre Dame might have had. They eventually got rewarded with a Summer Denigan goal off her chest from a Blum cross, tying her with Manning for the team lead in assists. That gave UNC a 4-1 lead that was too big to overcome.

As I mentioned, the Heels have an 8-game win streak that includes a 4-2 win over #6 Duke, a 3-1 win over #15 Virginia, and now this one. Devey's 14 and Denigan's 9 goals both rank within the country's top 10, and the defense has been suffocating, allowing opponents to shoot just 5.2 attempts per game. Nearly half of those are on target, so when they break, they've been breaking pretty hard, and making goalie Peyton Trayer's life difficult, leading to an unimpressive save percentage. Still, you'd rather a goalie have a low save percentage on few attempts than even a high one while facing a lot of shots. There's a reason this is the #1 team in the country.

They'll next face Florida State, with whom the Heels have jockeyed for the top spot in the ACC the past several years, and against whom UNC has lost their last three matchups. FSU's had a slow start to the year with a 4-1-3 record and 2 draws to open ACC play, but they're still dangerous, with a ranked win under their belts. That game will be on ESPNU next Friday night.

articles.title: Tait Reynolds is 2-0 as Clemson's starting QB. What to know about freshman vs Miami
articles.summary: Take a look at Tait Reynolds' path to becoming Clemson's QB as a freshman before the Tigers play Miami
articles.body:
CLEMSON — Clemson football freshman quarterback Tait Reynolds will make his first big start for the Tigers when he faces No. 4 Miami .

Clemson (3-1, 2-0 ACC) plays Miami (4-0, 2-0) on Oct. 3 (7:30 p.m., ABC). Reynolds was named the Tigers' starter by coach Dabo Swinney on Sept. 13, and he'll start his third game after victories over North Carolina and California.

Reynolds has passed for 521 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. He's completed 64.3% of his passes and has 83 rushing yards. Reynolds' quarterback rating of 29.0 is the lowest in the ACC.

Take a look at Reynolds' path from high school to now.

Tait Reynolds, Clemson football freshman quarterback for Dabo Swinney

Reynolds was born and raised in Queen Creek, Arizona, where he was the second-youngest of six children. He attended Queen Creek High School.

Reynolds has two older brothers who play college football: Utah linebacker Trey Reynolds and UT-Martin linebacker Porter Reynolds. He also has a younger sister, Emma, who plays high school softball and is committed to Oklahoma. Reynolds' father, Paul, was a linebacker at Arizona State from 1996-97.

Reynolds threw for 1,808 yards and 11 touchdowns and rushed for 631 yards and 17 touchdowns as a high school sophomore in 2023. He threw for 2,238 yards and 22 touchdowns and rushed for 1,426 yards and 19 touchdowns to earn first-team all-state honors and Arizona Player of the Year honors from the Arizona Cardinals as a junior in 2024. A hamstring injury kept Reynolds out for most of his senior season.

Reynolds also plays baseball as an outfielder and shortstop. He was named a 2025 Under Armour All-American and won an Arizona 6A baseball state title in 2024, hitting a walk-off single in the championship game .

Reynolds was a three-star recruit in the 247Sports Composite, a 2025 Elite 11 finalist and ESPN's No. 11 dual-threat quarterback in the Class of 2026. He's also committed to the Tigers for baseball.

How Tait Reynolds became Clemson's starting quarterback

Reynolds played well in spring football and scored a rushing touchdown in Clemson's spring game. He also completed 7 of 10 passes for 74 yards. However, senior Christopher Vizzina was still Swinney's starter.

Reynolds closed the gap on Vizzina in fall practice. Swinney even said before the game against LSU on Sept. 5 that there was a time when he thought Reynolds would win the job, which is exactly what he did after two games.

Vizzina's struggles drove Swinney to name Reynolds the starter the day after he played the majority of Clemson's 22-7 win over Georgia Southern due to Vizzina's elbow injury. Reynolds finished 16-for-27 for 178 passing yards, added 38 rushing yards and lost a fumble.

Swinney said his decision to start Reynolds was performance-based.

"Based on opportunity and mistakes and just body of work ... Tait has earned the opportunity to start," Swinney said.

Reynolds then helped the Tigers rally from 17-3 down against North Carolina on Sept. 19 with three second-half touchdown drives, including two in the fourth quarter after a long weather delay, to help Clemson win 28-20. That prompted Swinney to say Reynolds would "absolutely" be the Tigers' starter .

Reynolds finished 20-of-29 for 215 passing yards, one touchdown, and one interception against the Tar Heels.

"He's a competitor, and you saw it ... Some big-time plays in a big environment," Swinney said. "You're down 17-3, and everything's against you. To just have the toughness to keep believing, it's hard to coach that. It's hard to coach what he has."

What Tait Reynolds said before the Miami game

Reynolds said on Sept. 30 that games are slowing down for him the more he starts, and that they're beginning "to feel like practice more and more." He isn't feeling pressure to have his best game against Miami .

"I don't feel any pressure at all ... I'm not putting any pressure on myself," Reynolds said. "That's kind of something that's made up in my mind, and I'm not really worried about anything. Just trust the guys around me. Trust them to do their job. Try to do mine."

He's also trying not to make the moment too big.

"You just stay focused on the process," Reynolds said. "Whatever happens, the good or the bad, at the end of the day, I'm just a disciple of Jesus Christ, and I just try to be that all the time. My identity's not football. I think sometimes bad things happen; they're going to happen, and it just gives you a great opportunity to grow and learn and get better."

articles.title: Kyle Shanahan explains why 49ers keep welcoming back former players
articles.summary: Deebo Samuel, Dre Greenlaw and Dante Pettis all returned to the 49ers after spent at least the past season on other teams.
articles.body:
Kyle Shanahan has never been shy about a reunion. With Deebo Samuel and Dre Greenlaw back in San Francisco and Dante Pettis now on the practice squad, the San Francisco 49ers head coach explained in an interview with NBC Sports Bay Area's Matt Maiocco that the door stays open because of the type of players they are.

"It was their home," Shanahan said of players returning to San Francisco. "It's where they started out. They went other places. Whatever happened there doesn't really matter, but I think that they were excited to come back and I know how excited we were to get them back."

Samuel and Greenlaw were selected in the 2019 draft and spent their first six seasons in San Francisco. Both then left: Greenlaw signed with the Denver Broncos during the 2025 offseason, and Samuel was traded to the Washington Commanders after requesting a deal. After one year away, each returned on a one-year contract in 2026.

Samuel caught 77 passes for 727 yards and five touchdowns for the Commanders in 2025, but his play declined over the season and Washington decided not to bring him back. Shanahan, meanwhile, wasn't confident the 49ers could bring him back because of interest from elsewhere. But after a litany of receiver injuries decimated the offense, a reunion made sense for both sides.

"I thought he was going to end up somewhere else, but we did watch him on tape, and when you put the tape together, you see Deebo," Shanahan said. "You could see in Washington that he still had the same skill set ... we thought on tape last year, we didn't see a guy who had changed. It looked like the Deebo we had always known."

Greenlaw, meanwhile, left after the Broncos offered him a deal he knew the 49ers couldn't match. But his 2025 season didn't go as planned after a significant quad injury sidelined him until Week 7, and a hamstring issue later ended his regular season. He was also suspended for one game and was eventually released after 43 combined tackles, one sack and one interception in eight games.

Pettis is an even more recent example, after only coming back this week after being away from the team since 2020. The 49ers took him in the second round of the 2018 draft, but he was eventually waived and bounced around the league, spending time with four different teams. San Francisco signed him to the practice squad on Tuesday.

The reunions have worked out well for Samuel and Greenlaw, while Pettis hasn't seen the field yet for San Francisco. Samuel has nine receptions for 159 yards and two scores, while Greenlaw has 22 tackles combined.

articles.title: CMU launches branded beer. Where to find it now

articles.body:
Central Michigan University this week announced it has launched a new branded beer that will be served at Kelly/Shorts Stadium and a Midland brewery.

The school on Thursday, Oct. 1, said it was launching Central 1892, a traditional American ale, in partnership with Van Wagner, and Midland Brewing Company. Fabiano Brothers Distributing will serve as the distribution partner for this initiative.

"This is an exciting moment for our department and university as months of collaboration have led to this first-of-its-kind product launch for our fans," Zyzlewski Family Vice President and Director of Athletics Amy Folan said.

CMU introduced the new beer during its home game on Saturday, Oct. 3, against Akron University. After Oct. 3, Central 1892 will be available at Midland Brewing Company and other restaurants and retail locations throughout Mount Pleasant and Midland.

CMU described the beer as an American traditional ale "with a light malt backbone and balanced hop bitterness."

Midland Brewing Company is the exclusive brewing partner for Central 1892, the university said.

"We are beyond thrilled to partner with Central Michigan Athletics and the University on this initiative," Midland Brewing Company Owner Dave Kepler said. "Our brewery is proud to support Central Michigan Athletics as we have other local companies and causes. It brings us great joy to bring this concept to life for CMU Chippewa alumni and fans to enjoy."

articles.title: Ben Whittaker vs Conor Wallace: Live blog, round-by-round updates and results
articles.summary: Ben Whittaker returns against Conor Wallace in Birmingham!
articles.body:
Ben Whittaker returns to action today for a possible final step ahead of a world title fight, as he faces Conor Wallace in what is an IBF title eliminator.

The flashy, controversial Whittaker will be a heavy favorite in the matchup with Australia's Wallace, and we'll also see British title fights at super welterweight and flyweight, plus the pro debut of super welterweight Odel Kamara .

We'll be here with live results and updates for the entire main card, plus round-by-round for the main event. Join us today!

Whittaker vs Wallace live blog and results

Odel Kamara def. Thodoris Ritzakis by TKO

Probably didn't need to be stopped. Not the greatest debut but debuts are generally sort of useless. A kid with butterflies tried too hard to get the KO, he'll be calmer having gotten this over with.

Uddin wins British and Commonwealth flyweight titles

Uddin (8-0, 5 KO) was just the better fighter, no two ways about it. He was better than the game Bruce (8-3, 0 KO) all the way through. Bruce was down twice in the fifth and just took a beating. Uddin is not going to win over neutrals with his attitude and personality, but the guy is a class above the domestic scene at 112.

Fawaz retains British super welterweight title

James (17-3, 0 KO) fought OK and gave Fawaz a good challenge, but Fawaz is just really hard to fight at this level. He brings so much energy, it's just really hard to keep him at bay for 12 rounds, and most of his opponents at this level aren't going to have the power or conditioning to figure that out. James doesn't have power, and he folded not out of lacking effort or toughness, he was just worn out. He went down twice in Round 8 and that was that.

Ibraheem Sulaimaan def. Sonny Hardy by unanimous decision

Official Scores: 96-93, 97-93, 97-93 for Sulaimaan

A notably terrific Round 7 and a damn good fight in all. But that 7th round charge might have pretty much done Hardy in, too. Still, he gave this a tremendous effort, gave himself a chance to win, and he just came up short. Sulaimaan is now 12-0 (5 KO), while Hardy drops to 12-1 (5 KO).

articles.title: Couch: 3 quick takes on Michigan State football's 31-3 loss at Wisconsin
articles.summary: Graham Couch of the Lansing State Journal offers three quick takes from Michigan State's 31-3 loss to Wisconsin.
articles.body:
MADISON, Wis. — Graham Couch of the Lansing State Journal offers three quick takes from Michigan State's 31-3 loss to Wisconsin .

1. MSU looks so far away from winning games like this

You can argue that the last great era of Michigan State football officially died at Camp Randall Stadium seven years ago. Saturday's wellness check — the first visit since — showed a fairly weak pulse.

The Spartans look so far away from winning games like this. They just don't win many individual matchups. And, discouragingly, Wisconsin isn't a team with overwhelming talent, either. But the differences were enough Saturday — a quarterback the Spartans ' couldn't stop on the move, playmakers good enough to execute on third downs, a defensive line MSU couldn't quite handle in pass protection, and defensive backs the Spartans ' receivers couldn't separate from.And thus a final score, 31-3, fitting of the game that took place.

I don't know how it gets better this season. The Spartans can move the ball between the 30s well enough, but struggle to push it into the red zone, let alone convert once there. They can run it up the gut with varying degrees of efficiency, though struggled on key downs Saturday, turning it over five times on fourth-down tries. They've got an emerging tight end in Jayden Savoury , but otherwise no one else that seems remotely able to be featured in the passing game. They've got a capable kicker and punter. But they can't be the bones of a successful team. And they've got injuries to key guys — including their one difference-maker on offense — without the depth to withstand it.They've got nothing right now on offense. You have to score to win in this game. They've scored a combined 26 points in three games against high-major competition this season and 19 points in their last three visits to Wisconsin, including a 38-0 defeat in 2019 that told us better days under Mark Dantonio weren't coming back.

Worse yet, for Spartan fans, anger gets you nothing. There's no head to put on a stake. This is the first season of a head coach in Pat Fitzgerald who MSU desperately needs to succeed. Besides, everyone to be mad at is no longer at MSU.Apathy doesn't help, either. The ability to find satisfaction in basketball season as early as November is one of MSU's challenges as a football program. Folks, donors included, only have to suffer for so long, before they can replace the frustration with the trill of Tom Izzo's men's basketball program.

And so the only choice is to endure and hope what's a relatively old roster keeps playing hard, that a defense — which isn't great but isn't the problem — doesn't let the dam break, that MSU's young QB finds a level he hasn't shown in recent weeks, that the offensive line gets/stays healthy and finds a groove, and that Savoury becomes a guy who's a problem in the passing game, and that somebody else does, too.

Otherwise, there are going to be many more days like this.

2. Savoury not a savior but increasingly good

For four weeks, we've seen signs that MSU tight end Jayden Savoury could be a difference-maker, including an incredible almost-catch against Nebraska. Saturday at Wisconsin, the 6-foot-5, 250-pound redshirt freshman was MSU's most reliable target and a player the coaches clearly think is worth featuring — and he finished with just four catches for 26 yards. It felt like more. Perhaps that's because so much offensively was a struggle for the Spartans and 21 of his yards came on three catches on MSU's lone scoring drive. That felt like something.

It's tough for a tight end to be a primary weapon. But if and when MSU ever gets one again at the wideout position, Savoury has the look of a guy who could be a heckuva complementary piece and target for MSU's quarterback. Something to consider for next season.

3. MSU's defense didn't execute the most important part of the scouting report

The Spartans' defense might not be the primary problem, but its inability to execute what had to be the top line item in the scouting report contributed to this lopsided defeat.

The key to limiting Wisconsin's offense is to limit Badgers ' QB Colton Joseph in the running game. Instead, Joseph had 41 yards on four runs on the game's first five plays, setting the stage for a 13-play 75-yard touchdown drive. On the Badgers' next possession, Joseph's 26-yard run was the long play on another touchdown drive. In all, he carried 13 times for 141 yards, including a 47-yard touchdown run.

MSU's defense had some moments, but failed at the primary objective and also on key downs when the game was still in doubt, allowing the Badgers to convert on 7 of 10 third and fourth downs in the first half, while building a 17-3 lead at the break.

MSU won't win another game with those sort of inefficiencies on defense.

Contact Graham Couch at gcouch@lsj.com. Follow him on X @Graham_Couch and BlueSky @GrahamCouch.

articles.title: Jaguars add LB and CB to Week 4 game-day roster v. Bengals
articles.summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars are elevating two players to the Week 4 game-day roster.
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars are elevating two players from the practice squad to the game-day roster for the team's Week 4 matchup with the Cincinnati Bengals .

Linebacker Jalen McLeod and cornerback Jabbar Muhammad will be available for Sunday's game.

This will be McLeod's third and final practice squad elevation. Moving forward, if the Jaguars want him available on game days, he will have to be signed to the 53-man roster.

McLeod has filled a special-teams-heavy role over the last two weeks, playing 20 combined snaps, primarily on the kick return and kick coverage units.

Muhammad's elevation comes as the Jaguars are dealing with injuries at cornerback . Both Montaric Brown (hamstring) and Christian Braswell (knee) are questionable.

He put together a strong showing during training camp, and the Jaguars' decision to release him during cutdowns was a bit of a surprise.

If Muhammad is called upon on Sunday, he will provide depth on defense and could be tasked with filling more of a special teams role.

This is Muhammad's first elevation of the 2026 season. He has two more remaining.

articles.title: Western Michigan goes ahead late in the fourth, holds on for victory when Buffalo goes for the win
articles.summary: (AP) — Dieter Kelly kicked the go-ahead field goal with 79 seconds remaining and the Western Michigan defense held on fourth-and-goal with two seconds left i...
articles.body:
BUFFALO, N.Y. (AP) — Dieter Kelly kicked the go-ahead field goal with 79 seconds remaining and the Western Michigan defense held on fourth-and-goal with two seconds left in a 20-17 victory over Buffalo on Saturday in the Mid-American Conference opener for both teams.

After Kelly's field goal gave the Broncos their 20-17 lead, Buffalo drove 74 yards and faced fourth-and-goal from the 2-yard line. The Bulls went for the win and quarterback Jason Wright was stopped short by Scoop Gardner Jr. as he raced to the pylon.

Buffalo led 14-10 at halftime after a 59-yard touchdown pass from Wright to Patrick Clacks III and a 1-yard touchdown run by Messiah Burch.

After a scoreless third quarter, Buffalo went ahead 17-10 on Oliver Hautanen's 35-yard field goal. The Broncos then rallied with Broc Lowry's 5-yard touchdown run and Kelly's 38-yard field goal with 1:19 remaining.

Lowry completed 19 of 24 passes for 212 yards and added 54 yards rushing, including the tying touchdown in the fourth quarter. Jalen Buckley had a touchdown and 62 yards rushing for the Broncos (3-2).

Wright was 11-of-18 passing for 170 yards and Burch had 106 yards rushing for the Bulls (2-3).

Western Michigan holds a 10-2 lead in the series.

The Bulls had won their previous four Mid-American Conference openers.

articles.title: Lakers have made defense a major emphasis in training camp
articles.summary: The Lakers’ physical start to training camp reflects a defensive approach built on aggressive perimeter play and Kessler’s protection at the rim.
articles.body:
Los Angeles — Defense has been an early priority for the Lakers in training camp, and their wings are setting not just the tone but the standard.

The effort and physicality during Wednesday's practice prompted JJ Redick to shorten portions of the session. Redick said the wings were the ones establishing that physicality, disrupting possessions early and maintaining pressure away from the ball.

By Friday, Ziaire Williams said that effort was creating expectations across the roster.

"We got some dogs on this team," Williams said. "Everyone plays 1-4. All the wings are great. There's no slack; you see four or five wings out there playing hard, everybody else has to pick it up a notch."

Williams' assessment echoed Walker Kessler's confidence in a group he believes is being overlooked defensively.

"We're going to be a nasty defensive team, I'm just being honest," Kessler said this week. "We're going to be really good defensively. We have a lot of defensive tools."

Last season, the Lakers finished 20th in defensive efficiency. Improving that standing will require their new personnel to work together, connecting pressure on the perimeter with protection around the basket.

Quentin Grimes outlined his part in that approach at Monday's Media Day. Conversations with Redick and assistant coach Greg St. Jean have focused on returning to the defensive responsibilities he carried early in his career with New York.

Alongside Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves, Grimes can concentrate on defending opposing ball handlers and helping establish the intensity the Lakers want.

"Bringing that intensity, bringing that nastiness," Grimes said on Media Day.

He identified Collin Sexton, Matisse Thybulle and Williams as teammates who can help make the Lakers one of the toughest, hardest-playing teams defensively.

Thybulle's production offers an example of that disruptive potential.

He averaged 2.0 steals in just 16.0 minutes per game with Portland last season. Injuries limited him to 30 appearances, but his ability to create turnovers gives the Lakers another way to interrupt an opponent's offense.

Now we haven't even gotten to the Lakers' biggest defensive piece they acquired this offseason in Kessler.

Kessler brings an established shot-blocking anchor to a team seeking elite defending inside.

In 2024-25, his last full season available, he averaged 2.4 blocks, ranking second in the NBA. A shoulder injury limited him to five games last season, so that earlier campaign provides a more substantial measure of his production.

Grimes said having Kessler behind him allows him to crowd ball handlers and defend with greater physicality. Beating the first defender would still leave an opponent facing a difficult finish.

"If you beat me, you got to see Walker at the rim," Grimes said.

Kessler sees the relationship working both ways. A perimeter defender who stays on a driver's hip helps him contest the shot rather than confront an attacker with an open path to the basket.

That cooperation matters as Redick evaluates combinations and players compete for starting roles. Grimes said he "100%" wants to start and welcomed the competition.

"I want to fight for it. I want to earn it," he said.

The Lakers are counting on their perimeter defenders and Kessler to bring out the best in each other. Pressure on the ball can make his job easier inside, while his presence at the rim gives the wings confidence to defend aggressively.

That connection is central to the defense they are working to establish in camp, making for an anticapitating combination with Dončić's elite scoring.

articles.title: Daniel Gafford Finally Ready To Hit Threes For Dallas
articles.summary: Daniel Gafford admits he never shot threes in college but is embracing a new role with the Mavericks. Here is why this change matters for Dallas.
articles.body:
Daniel Gafford is done with just dunking. The Dallas Mavericks center is finally ready to stretch the floor, a shift that changes everything for their offense. This isn't a small tweak; it is a major upgrade for a team that needs spacing to win.

Gafford has only taken one three-pointer in his entire NBA career. That single attempt happened during a game with the Washington Wizards back in the 2021-22 season. He remembers it as a desperate heave before the clock ran out. Now, he is expected to do it on purpose. On Sunday, Coach Dusty May informed reporters that Gafford will take rhythm threes provided he merits the privilege of continuing to do so.

Gafford admitted the change feels strange at first. "But, I mean, I'm looking forward to it. They're putting a lot of faith in me to be able to take those shots, so it's only right that I do the same for myself," he said. He knows the first few will likely miss. That is fine. The goal is to build the confidence to keep taking the next step.

His background makes this jump even more impressive. While at Arkansas, his role remained straightforward: setting screens, rolling toward the basket, catching lobs, and rebounding. "I did not. No. I took maybe a couple of jump shots in college, but that's pretty much it. I didn't shoot no threes at all," Gafford said. He spent most of his time dunking the ball. Now, he is growing as a player and learning to add a new weapon to his game.

The Mavericks signed him to a three-year, $54.4 million contract extension ahead of the 2026-27 season. That is a lot of money to bet on a player learning to shoot. But the team sees the value. If Gafford can hit even a few of these shots, the defense has to respect him at the top of the key. This opens up driving lanes for Cooper and Kyrie.

Max Christie noted that confidence is the biggest thing for Gafford's shot. The center is aware of the risk. "I mean, it's going to feel good, I would say. Hopefully it just doesn't go to my head and I start jacking up threes," Gafford said. He wants to be smart about it. The team just needs him to keep the faith and knock down the open looks when they come.

articles.body:
Match will be broadcast on CBF TV Credits: Nelson Terme /CBF

Brazil's Under-20 National Team takes the field this Sunday (4) for its final fixture of the FIFA international window in Spain. After beating Denmark 4-1 and the United States 2-0, Brazil will face Mexico at 11 a.m. local time (6 a.m. Brasília time) at Pinatar Arena in San Pedro del Pinatar.

Coached by Paulo Victor, the team heads into the match with two wins in two games. The time in Spain has helped the coaching staff continue their work and test the squad against opponents from different footballing backgrounds.

In the opening match, Brazil defeated Denmark 4-1, with goals from Bruninho, Lucas Rodrigues, Heittor, and Yuri Leles. The forward, who scored in the first match, highlighted the importance of the experience with the national team and the run of games.

Against the United States, the team won again, this time 2-0, with goals from Igor Felisberto and Heittor. The match was more evenly contested and required a response from Brazil after a first half in which the Americans had more control.

For Yuri Leles, the team is prepared for the final challenge of the stretch.

"I think we're very well prepared to go out there again tomorrow, play a great match against Mexico, and finish strong."

Mexico will be Brazil's final opponent during this spell in Spain. The match will be broadcast on CBF TV.

articles.title: Keenan Allen downgraded to out for Week 4
articles.summary: Colts WR Keenan Allen was downgraded to out and won't play in Week 4 against Commanders
articles.body:
Indianapolis Colts WR Keenan Allen (groin) was downgraded to OUT on Saturday, Oct. 3. for Week 4's game in London against the Washington Commanders . Allen was initially listed as questionable on the Colts' final injury report after two limited practices and a DNP on Friday.

Why It Matters: Allen seems to have suffered a groin injury at practice this week, and it was bad enough to rule him out the day before Indianapolis faces the Commanders in London on Sunday morning. Allen has been a useful low-end flex so far this season for fantasy, but this injury puts a bit of a damper on his early-season success thus far.

articles.title: Alabama State football vs Bethune-Cookman in weather delay
articles.summary: Weather hit Daytona Stadium late in the first quarter of Alabama State football vs. Bethune-Cookman, placing the game in a weather delay.
articles.body:
What started as an overcast beginning to the first quarter quickly became a downpour of rain in Daytona Stadium.

Alabama State football was facing a third-and-long with 19 seconds left in the first quarter before officials stopped play and sent teams to the locker rooms for a weather delay.

According to NCAA guidelines, a college football game faces immediate mandatory suspension when lightning is detected within an 8-mile radius. Officials must wait 30-minutes before play resumes. If lighting strikes within the 8-mile radius before time expires, the 30-minute clock restarts.

Bethune-Cookman has possessed the ball twice and both times have managed to drive into Alabama State 's red zone. The Hornet defense has managed to hold the Wildcat offense on third-and-short to two field goals.

Alabama State's lackluster offense has been an issue this season. It's the second consecutive game starting quarterback Andrew Body has missed with a bone injury in his non-throwing wrist. True freshman Aaron Frye is getting his second start, and so far, it's been a rough go for the freshman.

When play resumes, Alabama State will have the ball third-and-9 on its own 25-yard line with 19 seconds left in the first quarter.
